title: Cabin Window Frame Corrosion Removal and Bonded Repair
abstract: Repair of corrosion in the cabin window frame land, covering removal to sound material, the bonded reinforcement and the pressure test that must follow before the aircraft is returned to service.

sections.purpose: Repair of corrosion found in the cabin window frame land, by removal to sound material followed by a bonded reinforcement, with a pressure test as the acceptance step.
sections.damage_assessment: Corrosion is found in the frame land under the window seal, typically on aircraft operating in coastal or humid environments, and it is not visible until the window assembly is removed. The assessment must establish the depth of attack after cleaning, because the remaining land thickness governs whether the bonded repair is applicable or whether the frame must be replaced. Pitting deeper than the stated limit at any point takes the frame out of this scheme. The seal groove profile must be checked after removal: a groove that no longer holds the seal profile cannot be restored by the bonded repair and produces a leak path that the pressure test will find but the visual inspection will not.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the window assembly and the seal in accordance with the removal task. Clean the frame land and remove all corrosion product. Remove corrosion to sound material by mechanical means, keeping within the depth limit and blending the removal area smoothly into the surrounding land. Measure and record the remaining thickness at the four positions given on repair drawing RD-56-20-11-003. Prepare the bonded surface to the surface preparation standard. Bond the reinforcement ring D5620113496156 into the removal area and cure under the schedule given. Install the retaining item D5620110905714 and the seal seat D5620116475200 with fasteners AES808479K3. Restore the protective treatment and the sealant. Reinstall the window assembly with a new seal. Do the cabin pressure test at the level given in the figure and confirm no leakage at the repaired frame.
sections.inspection_requirements: Visual inspection of the bonded area for edge lift before the window is reinstalled. Cabin pressure test at the stated level with a leak check at the repaired frame. A repeat visual inspection of the repaired frame is required at every window seal replacement, and in any case not more than 8 000 flight hours apart. The remaining thickness measurements must be retained; a subsequent corrosion finding at the same frame is assessed against them and not against the nominal thickness.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Corrosion depth up to 0.8 mm after removal, over an area not exceeding one quarter of the frame land circumference, with no pitting deeper than 0.4 mm outside the removal area.

repair_drawings.title: Bonded reinforcement ring, cabin window frame land

type_data.fastener_pattern: Sixteen blind rivets at 30 degree spacing around the reinforcement ring, 10 mm edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Not life limited. The repaired frame is re-inspected at every window seal replacement and the remaining thickness record governs any later corrosion assessment at the same frame.
